UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2154 
ANSWERED ON 14.03.2023 
 
BATTERY SWAPPING TRANSFORM URBAN MOBILITY 
 
2154. SHRI KURUVA GORANTLA MADHAV:  
DR. BEESETTI VENKATA SATYAVATHI:  
 
Will the Minister of HEAVY INDUSTRIES भारी उद्योग मंत्री be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether battery swapping transform urban mobility would bring a shift in favour of 
Electric Vehicle adoption;  
 
(b) if so, the initiatives  of the Government and Public Sector Undertaking (PSU) in this 
regard;  
 
(c) whether battery swapping will lead to increase in generation of electronic waste and if so, 
the manner in which the Government proposes to deal with the issue; and  
 
(d) if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR HEAVY INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI KRISHAN PAL GURJAR) 
 
 
(a) & (b):  Sir, NITI Aayog has uploaded a draft policy on their website for stakeholders’  
consultation for implementing the battery swapping policy.  With battery swapping policy, faster 
adoption of EVs will take place which will increase public confidence in EVs. 
 
Battery swapping is generally used for smaller vehicles such as 2Ws and 3Ws with  
smaller batteries that are easier to swap, compared to 4 wheelers and e -buses, although solutions 
are emerging for the latter segments as well.   Battery swapping offers three key advantages 
relative to charging : it is time, space, and cost efficient, prov ided each swappable battery is 
actively used. 
 
(c) & (d):  As per the information received from Ministry of Environment, Forest and 
Climate Change, Government of India published the Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022 on 
24th August, 2022 for environmenta lly sound management of waste batteries, including EV 
batteries.  
 
The rules provide Extended Producer Responsibility framework for producers of batteries 
to recycle/ refurbish the waste batteries as per the prescribed timelines. Further, the rules 
mandate the recyclers to recover the minimum percentage of materials from waste batteries.

2155. SHRIMATI QUEEN OJA: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the number of women constables and sub -inspectors posted in police 
stations across the country with district-wise; 
 
(b) whether there is any limit fixed for the  number of women constables in 
the police station and if so, the details thereof; 
 
(c) whether there has been different limit  earmarked in each State in this 
regard and, if so, the details thereof, State-wise; 
 
(d) whether the Government has also set up  some women police stations in 
each State and if so, the details thereof, State-wise and district-wise; 
 
(e) the number of women police station in -charges posted in police stations 
across the country  and the number of women police station in -charges 
posted in the State of Assam; and 
 
(f) whether the Government is consideri ng to increase the number of women 
police station in-charges and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI NITYANAND RAI) 
(a) to (c) “Police” is a State subject falling in List -II (State List) of seventh 
schedule of the Constitution of India. It is primarily the responsibility of the 
State Governments/UTs to increase the number of women personnel in police 
forces. The Central Government advises the States/UTs from time to time. 

-2- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 2155 FOR 14.03.2023 
 
The Ministry of Home Affairs has issued advisories from time to time  to all 
the State Governments to increase the representation of women police to 
33% of the total strength. All the State Governments have been requested to 
create additional posts of women Constables/Sub -Inspectors by converting 
the vacant posts of Constab les/Sub-Inspectors. The aim is that each police 
station should have at least 3 women Sub -Inspectors and 10 women police 
Constables, so that a women help desk is manned round the clock. The 
district-wise data relating to number of women constables and sub -
inspectors posted in police stations across the country is not maintained 
centrally. However, as per the data compiled by Bureau of Police Research & 
Development (BPR&D), as on 01.01.2022, the actual strength of women 
police personnel is 11.75% at all India level. 
(d) to (f)  “Police” being a State subject, it is for the States/UTs to set up 
women police stations in their respective State/UT and to post women police 
station in-charges. The district-wise and State-wise data of number of women 
police station in-charges posted in police stations are not maintained 
centrally. However, as per  data compiled by BPR&D, as on 01.01.2022,

agricultural produce, better supply chain and market linkages, etc.

MILK FEDERATIONS AND UNIONS 
 
2160. SHRI MOHANBHAI KALYANJI KUNDARIYA: 
 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING  
मत्स्यपालन, पशुपालन और डेयरी  मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is the fact that there are a number of milk defunct cooperative milk  federations and 
unions in the country; 
(b) if so, the details along with the capacity thereof in the country, State and district-wise; 
(c) whether the Government has any action plan to revive those defunct milk federations and 
unions; 
(d) if so, the time likely to be taken for their revival; and 
(e) if not, the reasons therefor? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER FOR FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI PARSHOTTAM RUPALA) 
 
(a) & (b) Based on the information provided by National Dairy Development Board, there are 281 
Milk Unions/Marketing or Metro Dairies/State Federation or Apex Bodies in the country, of which 
20 Milk Federation/ Unions are currently defunct/non-functional. The details are at Annexure. 
(c) & (d) Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying  (DAHD), Government of India is 
implementing the following schemes primarily focusing on development of cooperative dairy sector 
including cooperative milk federations and unions . These schemes/projects of DAHD are oriented 
towards supporting  these cooperatives  with working capital, strengthening of milk chilling and 
processing capacities etc. 
(i) National Programme for Dairy Development (NPDD): 
NPDD scheme is being implemented ac ross the country since Feb -2014 with the objective of 
creating/strengthening infrastructure for production of quality milk, procurement, processing and 
marketing of milk & milk products by dairy cooperatives, milk producer companies and revival of 
dairy cooperative societies across the country. The scheme has been restructured/ realigned in July 
2021 for implementation during 2021-22 to 2025-26. 

Under Component B of NPDD scheme  (Dairying through Cooperatives), provision has been made 
to provide financial assistance for organisation/revival of dairy cooperatives  under “Strengthening 
of Milk Procurement Infrastructure” component.  
(ii) Dairy Processing and Infrastructure Development Fund (DIDF): 
DIDF was launched in December 2017 with the objective of creation/ strengthening of Milk 
Processing, Value addition & chilling facilities for Dairy  Cooperatives, Multi State Dairy 
Cooperatives, Milk Producer Companies (MPC), National Dairy Development Board’s (NDDBs) 
subsidiaries, Self Help Groups (SHGs) and Far mer Producer Organisations (FPOs) registered under 
State Cooperative and Companies Act. 
(iii) Supporting Dairy Cooperatives and Farmer Producer Organizations engaged in dairy 
activities (SDCFPO): 
SDCFPO is implemented as a part of umbrella Scheme “Infrastr ucture Development Fund” from 
2021-22 to 2025-26. The scheme is being implemented through National Dairy Development Board 
(NDDB) with the objective of assisting the cooperative societies and farmer producer organizations 
engaged in dairy activities by providing soft working capital. Due to Economic Impact of Covid -19 
on dairy sector, a new component “interest subvention on Working capital loans for Dairy sector” 
was introduced as one of the components. 
(e) Does not arise in view of above.

2161.  SHRI M.K. RAGHAVAN: 
            SHRI SHANMUGA SUNDARAM K.:   
 
Will the Minister of AGRICUL  TURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृषि एवं कक सान क ल्याण मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government plans to increase Minimum Support Price (MSP) for copra and if 
so, the details thereof;  
(b) whether the Government plans to increase the procurement prices for rubber through 
rubber board and if so, the details thereof;  
(c) whether the Government has noticed that there is a decline in agriculture productivity due 
to excessive usage of chemical fertilizers and if so, the details thereof and the steps taken by 
the Government to promote natural farming;  
(d) whether any incentives are being provided to farmers for purchase of seeds and other raw 
materials and if so, the details thereof; 
(e) whether the Government has observed that coconut yield per hectare has been coming 
down in Kerala and if so, the steps taken to improve the same; and  
(f) whether any financial incentives are provided to coconut farmers of Kerala and if so, the 
details regarding the same for Kerala district-wise? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
क ृषि एवं कक सान क ल्याण मंत्री  (SHRI NARENDRA SINGH TOMAR) 
 
(a) & (b): Government fixes Minimum Support Price (MSP) for 22 mandated agricultural 
crops and Fair & Remunerative Price (FRP) for sugarcane , on the basis of the 
recommendations of the Commission for Agr icultural Costs & Prices (CACP)  considering 

the views of State Governments and Central Ministries/ Departments concerned and other 
relevant factors.  Rubber is not amongst the mandated crops under MSP. The MSP for 
milling copra has been fixed at ₹ 10860/ - per quintal and for ball copra at ₹ 11750/ - per 
quintal for 2023 season . There is an increase of ₹270 per quintal for milling copra and 
₹750/- per quintal for ball copra over the previous season.  
 
(c):  As per Second Advance Estimates for 2022 -23, total foodgrain production in the 
country is estimated at  323.55 million tonnes which is  all time high .    Similarly, total 
horticulture production in the country is estimated at record of 342.33 million tonnes as per 
3rd Advance Estimate for 2021 -22. The record production, being a function of productivity, 
reflects pro -active efforts and farmer -friendly policies of government in the agriculture 
sector. Government is promoting natural farming through a sub -scheme namely Bharatiya 
Prakritik Paddhati (BPKP) under Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yajana (PKVY). Under BPKP, 
natural farming is bei ng promoted in cluster of 500 hectares  and ₹12200 per hectare  is 
provided for three years, in which ₹2000 is provided as incentives to farmers through 
Direct Benefit Transfer. Farmers are being encouraged to adopt natural farming by wide 
publicity through press and print media, publication of leaflets/booklets, organisation of 
workshops, exhibitions, farmers fairs etc.  
 
(d): Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare is im plementing Sub-Mission on Seeds 
& Planting Materials (SMSP ) from 2014 -15 to promote production and multiplication of 
quality seeds. Under SM SP, Seed  Village Programme is implemented to upgrade the 
quality of farmer’s saved seeds. Under the programme, financial assistance for 
foundation/certified seeds at 50% subsidy for cereal crop and 60% subsidy for pulses, 
oilseeds, fodder and green manure crops for production of quality seeds is provided for  
one acre per farmer.  In addition, financial assistance is also provided for different seed s 
related activities under other schemes viz. National Food Security Mission (NFSM) and 
Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana - Remunerative Approaches for Agriculture & All ied Sector 
Rejuvenation (RKVY-RAFTAAR) etc.  
 
(e) & (f): To improve the production and yield of coconut in the state of Kerala, Coconut

ALL WEATHER ROADS UNDER PMGSY-III 
 
2162.  SHRI PRADEEP KUMAR SINGH: 
SHRI JUGAL KISHORE SHARMA: 
SHRIMATI GEETA KORA: 
SHRI PARBATBHAI SAVABHAI PATEL: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the three years target of Pradhan  Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) from 
the year 2019 to 2022 under the third phase of the said yojana to achieve complete 
rural connectivity through all weather roads has been achieved; 
(b)  if so, the approximate percentage of houses  in all the States of the country, 
particularly in the States of Jammu and Kashmir, Jharkhand, Bihar and  Gujarat yet to 
be connected by all weather roads under the said yojana; 
(c)  whether the Ministry is aware that the said  yojana is essential for the overall socio -
economic development of various districts across the country; and 
(d)  if so, the details of the efforts being made by  the Ministry to achieve the said 
objective? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT  
(SADHVI NIRANJAN JYOTI) 
 
(a)  to (d)      Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana -III (PMGSY-III) was launched in the year 
2019 for consolidation of 1,25,000 Km Through Routes and Major Rural Links connecting 
habitations to Gramin Agricultural Markets (GrAMs), Higher Secondary Schools and 
Hospitals among other facilities. Since the inception of PMGSY -III till 07.03.2023, 99,319 
km road  length has been sanctioned, out of which, 51,851 km road length has been 
completed. The timeline of completion of PMGSY-III is March, 2025. 
The unit for PMGSY-I scheme is a habitation and not a house. All weather road connectivity 
to unconnected habitatio ns of designated population size as per census, 2001 was envisaged 
in PMGSY-I. 
  
The primary objective of the PMGSY -I is to provide connectivity, by way of an all -weather 
road with necessary culverts and cross -drainage structures, which is operable through out the 
year, to eligible unconnected habitations in rural areas. Habitations with a population of 500+ 
in plain areas and 250+ in North -Eastern and Himalayan states, Desert areas, Tribal 
(Schedule V) areas and selected tribal and backward districts as ide ntified by the Ministry of 
Home Affairs/ Planning Commission as per Census, 2001 were to be covered under the 
scheme, so that these habitations can have access to basic health services, education and 
markets for their produce. In the critical Left -Wing Ext remism (LWE) affected blocks (as 
identified by Ministry of Home Affairs), additional relaxation has been given to connect 
habitations with population of 100+ (Census 2001).  
 

 
The timeline for completion of PMGSY – I was March, 2019. However, on the demand of 
the states/UTs, the timeline for completion of the scheme was extended till September, 2022.  
Against 1,78,184 eligible habitations of 250+ and 500+ population size identif ied for 
coverage under the scheme, 16,086 habitations have been provided connectivity by the States 
out of their own resources and 4,815 habitations have either been dropped or have not been 
found feasible. Out of the balance 1,57,282 habitations sanctione d for providing connectivity 
under the PMGSY, 1,56,399 have already been covered. Thus, as on 7th   March, 2023, 883 
habitations remained to be connected. Hence, 99.44% habitations have been provided 
connectivity under PMGSY-I in 250+ population category.  
  
Further, under 100 -249 population category (LWE areas), out of sanctioned 6,253 
habitations, 5,999 habitations have been connected till 07.03.2022 and only 254 habitations 
are left to be connected. Hence, 96% habitations have been provided connectivity u nder 100-
249 population category (LWE areas).  
  
The State-wise details of habitation connectivity across various States/ UTs of the country are 
given at Annexure-I.

INCREASE IN RURAL WAGES 
 
2168.  SHRI  KOTHA PRABHAKAR REDDY: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether there has been nominal increase in rural wages but when calculated against 
the rate of inflation, the real rural wages have had a negative growth; and 
(b)  if so, the details thereof and the reasons therefor along with the corrective steps being 
taken in this regard? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT  
(SADHVI NIRANJAN JYOTI) 
 
(a) & (b):  As per the information shared by Labour Bureau, Ministry of Labour &  
Employment, the Labour Bureau compiles and maintains average daily wage rate data in 
respect of selected agricultural and non -agricultural occupations on the basis of the data 
collected by the Field Operation Division (FOD) of National Statistical Office (NSO), 
Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation from a fixed set of 600 sample villages 
spread over 20 States.  
  
Month-wise average daily wage rate in respect of Non -Agricultural Occupation along with 
the Consumer Price Index for Rural Labourers (CPI-RL) from January 2017 to 2022 is given 
at Annexure-I. 
  
As per Section 6 (1) of Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act 
(Mahatma Gandhi NREGA), 2005, the Central Government may by notification specify the 
wage rate for unskilled work fo r its beneficiaries. Accordingly, the Ministry of Rural 
Development notifies Mahatma Gandhi NREGA wage rate for every financial year for 
States/UTs. To compensate the Mahatma Gandhi NREGA workers against inflation, the 
Ministry of Rural Development revises the wage rate every financial year based on change in 
Consumer Price Index for Agricultural Labourers (CPI -AL). If the calculated wage rate of 
any State is coming lower than the wage rate of the previous financial year, it is being 
protected by maintainin g the previous financial year's wage rate. The revised wage rate is 
made applicable from 1st April of each financial year. However, State Governments can 
provide wages over and above the wage rate notified by the Central Government under 
Mahatma Gandhi NREGA.

REVISION OF ESTIMATED COST OF PROJECTS 
 
2170.  SHRI M. BADRUDDIN AJMAL: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Union Government has permitted the States to revise the estimated cost 
of projects under the Pradhan Mantri Gram SadakYojana (PMGSY) in order to 
accommodate increase in the prices of raw materials; 
(b)  if so, the number of States which have revised the estimated cost of various projects 
during each of the last five years and current year; and 
(c)  the details of the cost of such projects increased and decreased due to such revisions 
during the said period? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT  
(SADHVI NIRANJAN JYOTI) 
 
(a) to (c)  As per Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) Programme 
Guidelines, States prepare Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) based on their prevailing 
Schedule of  Rates (SoR).  Accordingly, the Ministry sanctions the proposals based on the 
cost estimate arrived at by the States as per the prevailing SoR.  
After a project has been sanctioned, the costs over and above the sanctioned cost, due to 
increase in material rate or revision of Schedule of Rates (SoR) are be borne by the States. If 
cost increases on account of time overrun, the extra cost will also have to be borne by the 
States. Details of such projects are not available centrally.

BENEFICIARIES OF DDU-GKY 
 
2171.  SHRI DILIP GHOSH: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the salient features of Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-
GKY); 
(b)  the number of beneficiaries of the Yojana during the last five years State and district-
wise particularly in West Bengal; and 
(c)  the amount of funds allocated, disbursed and utilised for the Yojana during the said 
period, State and district-wise particularly for West Bengal? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT  
(SADHVI NIRANJAN JYOTI) 
 
 
(a) The Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU -GKY) is a placement 
linked skill development program for rural poor youth under National Rural Livelihoods 
Mission (NRLM) being implemented since September, 2014. Rural Youth in the age group of 
15-35 years are covered under this sche me. DDU-GKY guidelines provide for earmarking of 
50% of the funds for SCs and STs and 15% for minorities. Further, one third beneficiaries of 
the respective categories including general category covered under the scheme should be 
women. 
DDU-GKY follows a 3-tier implementation architecture for implementation. National level is 
responsible for policy, funding of central share and technical support, while State Rural 
Livelihood Missions (SRLMs) / State Skills Missions (SSMs) are responsible for funding of 
State share, implementation and monitoring controls. Project Implementing Agencies (PIAs), 
which are mostly private training partners, are responsible for mobilization, training and 
placements. 
(b) The State -wise number of beneficiaries of DDU -GKY for the last  five years and current 
year is given at Annexure-I. District-wise information is not maintained by the Ministry of 
Rural Development. 
(c) DDU-GKY is a Central Sector Scheme and State -wise / District-wise budget allocation is 
NOT being made. The details of  State-wise funds released during the last five year and 
current year are given at Annexure-II.

National Sports University 
 
†2172.  SHRI SANJAY BHATIA: 
 SHRI RAJAN VICHARE:  
 
Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government proposes to establish the National Sports 
University in the States of Haryana and Maharashtra in order to make it 
the best sports centres of the country; 
 
(b) if so, the details thereof, if not, the reasons therefor; 
 
(c) whether the Government proposes to build an Olympic Park spread 
over ten acres for Karnal parliamentary constituency in coordination 
with the State Government so that training facilities could be provided 
to state level players from Karnal and Panipat to train them to become 
international players and win Olympic gold medals like Mr. Neeraj 
Chopra; and 
 
(d) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS 
 (SHRI ANURAG SINGH THAKUR) 
 
(a) & (b): Presently, there is no proposal under the consideration of the 
Government of India for establishing National Sports University in the 
States of Haryana and Maharashtra. ‘Sports’ being a State Subject, the 
responsibility to promote and develop sports in the country, including 
sports education, rests primarily with the respective State/UT 
Governments. The Union Government supplements their efforts by 

bridging critical gaps. The National Sports University (NSU) which has 
been set up at Imphal in the State of Manipur, caters to students and 
athletes from all States/UTs of the country. 
 
(c) & (d): No such proposal is presently under the consideration of the 
Government of India. ‘Sports’ being a State Subject, the responsibility to 
promote and develop sports in the country, including building sports  
infrastructure, rests primarily with the respective States/UT 
Governments. The Union Government supplements their efforts by 
bridging critical gaps. However, under the component “Creation and 
Upgradation of Sports Infrastructure” of the Khelo India Scheme, the 
Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports has sanctioned 293 sports 
infrastructure projects of various sports disciplines in different 
States/UTs of the country. The Ministry also implements various 
schemes for the development of sports and provide benefits/facilities 
among the youth across the country, viz: 
 
(i) Khelo India Scheme; (ii) Assistance to National Sports Federations; 
(iii) Special Awards to Winners in International Sports Events and their 
Coaches; (iv) National Sports Awards; (v) Pension to Meritorious 
Sportspersons; (vi) Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay National Sports Welfare 
Fund; (vii) National Sports Development Fund (NSDF); and (viii) Running 
Sports Training Centres through Sports Authority of India. 
 
The details of the above schemes are available in the public domain on 
the websites of this Ministry and the Sports Authority of India 
(www.yas.nic.in/sports; www.sportsauthorityofindia.nic.in).

क ृषि एवं ककसान  कल्याण मंत्री   (SHRI NARENDRA SINGH TOMAR) 
 
(a):  The survey on Situation Assessment of Agricultural Households and Land and Livestock 
Holdings of Households in Rural India , 2019  conducted by National Sample Survey Office 
(NSSO) provides data on  rural households classified by their major source s of income. As 
per this survey , about 58.3% of the rural households reported agricultural activities  as their 
main source of Income. As per Agriculture Census 2015 -16, small and marginal operational 
holders constituted about 86 per cent of the total operational holders in the country.  
 
(b) & (c ):  There is no proposal to introduce a separate budget for Agriculture. However, 
Government of India provides top most priority to the sector  which is the backbone of the 
economy. This is reflected in the fact that budget allocation for the Ministry of Agriculture and 
Farmers’ Welfare is very substantial. It has increased from Rs.27662.67 crore in 2013 -14 to 
Rs. 132513.62 crore in 2022-23.  
 
(d):  In 2017 -18, foodgrain production in India was estimated at 285.01 Million Tonnes 
(MT).As per information obtained from FAOSTAT(database of FAO), India’s production, 
consumption(domestic supply) and import of pulses in 2018 vis-à-vis the world  was 28%, 
30% and 14% respectively.

SUBSIDY ON EXPORT OF COTTON 
 
2174. SHRI RAMDAS C. TADAS: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृषि और कक सान क ल्याण मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government proposes to give subsidy on export of cotton on the lines 
of sugar to compensate the loss of cotton producers and exporters; 
 
(b) if so, the time by which it is likely to be implemented and if not, the reasons therefor; 
and 
 
(c) the details of measures being taken by the Government in the interest of farmers 
from Wardha, Nagpur, Yavatmal, Buldhana, Amravati of Vidarbha region pre -dominantly 
engaged in cotton production? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
क ृषि और कक सान क ल्याण मंत्री   (SHRI NARENDRA SINGH TOMAR) 
 
(a) & (b): At present, export subsidies are not available for cotton . However, rebate under 
Remission of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products (RoDTEP) scheme is available 
@3.1% of Freight On Board (FOB) value . The prices of Fair Average Quality (FAQ) grade 
seed cotton (kapas) in the domestic market  are ruling over MSP of Rs. 6080 (medium 
staple) and Rs. 6380 (long staple).  
 
(c): To safeguard the interest of the cotton farmers from Wardha, Nagpur, Yavatmal, 
Buldhana, Amravati, Cotton Corporation of India Limited  has opened 43 procurement 
centres. Further, Cotton Development programme  is being implemented under National 
Food Security Mission (NFSM) in 15 states including Maharashtra state since 2014 -15 to 
enhance production & productivity. Besides, state sponsored productivity and value chain 
development project on cotton is also being  implemented since 2022 -23, with focus on 
productivity enhancement of cotton, capacity building of farmers, strengthening of seed 
chain, value chain development and convergence with other ongoing schemes like farm 
pond, irrigation equipments & mechanization.

the responsibility of the State Governments.   However, in order to ensure that the roads 
constructed under PMGSY are maintained properly, following initiatives have been taken: 
(i)  All road works sanctioned under PMGSY are covered by initial five-year maintenance 
contracts to be entered into along with the construction contract, with the same contractor, as 
per the Standard Bidding Document.

Governments and placed at the disposal of the State Rural Roads Development Agencies

maintenance, PMGSY roads are required to be placed under Zonal maintenance contracts 
consisting of 5 -year maintenance including renewal as per maintenance cycle, from time to 
time, to be funded by the State governments.

States have to enter into a Memorandum  of Understanding with the Ministry of Rural 
Development, Government of India before launching of the scheme for providing adequate 
funds for maintenance of roads constructed/ upgraded under PMGSY during initial five years 
for routine maintenance, and for further five -year routine maintenance including periodic 
renewal as per requirement.

Officer of SRRDA is taken at the time of release of second installment of th e Programme 
Fund to the effect that Maintenance funds required as per maintenance contracts in force had

2177. SHRI ASADUDDIN OWAISI: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether National Human Rights Commission  has directed States and UTs 
to submit an  action taken report as to why patients cured  for mental illness 
are being kept illegally in  hospitals as they were to be sent to homes or half  
homes; 
 
(b) if so, whether Director General of Health Services has submitted report to 
the Commission  in regard to framing rules under Mental Healthcare  rules 
2017 as contemplated under Section 121 of the Act; 
 
(c) whether Commission has also directed DGs  of Police to submit report in 
respect of complaints  registered regarding mentally ill persons regarding  
non-rehabilitation or non-reintegration with families; and 
 
(d) if so, the details of reports received by NHRC and action taken or advisory 
issued to Health Ministry and Police in this regard? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI NITYANAND RAI) 
(a): As per the information provided by the National Human Rights 
Commission (NHRC),  the NHRC had issued notices to the Chief Secretaries 
and Principal Secretaries, Health, of all the State Governments as well as 
Administrators of Union Territories to submit a detailed action taken report 
on the issue of keeping the mentally cured patients even after recovery for 
inordinate period in contravention of Section 19 of Mental Health Act, 2017. 

-2- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 2177 FOR 14.03.2023 
 
(b):  Notices have been issued to the Secretary, Ministry of Health and Family 
Welfare, Government of India and Director General of Health Services, New 
Delhi, seeking the report on s tatus of framing rules under the Act 2017 as 
well as establishment of the Central Authority as contemplated under 
Section 33 of the Act 2017.  
(c) to (d): As per the information provided by the NHRC, the NHRC has also 
directed DGs of Police to submit repor t with regard to the status of the 
complaints received or registered relating to mentally ill persons, regarding

proposed to be taken to ensure that cured persons from mental illness should 
be living with the family and  other members of the community;  assistance or 
other measures taken from District Legal Services Authority or State Legal 
Services Authority, as the case may be. Requisite reports in response to 
notice have not been received from the concerned authorities so far.

RURAL WOMEN UNDER DAY-NRLM 
 
2178. MS. S. JOTHIMANI: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the number of rural women residing in the State of Tamil Nadu particularly in the 
Karur Constituency that received assistance and were mobilised into Self -Help 
Groups (SHGs) under the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana -National Rural Livelihoods 
Mission (DAY-NRLM); 
(b)  the amount of funds allocated and released under the yojana to Tamil Nadu since 
2014, year-wise; 
(c)  the steps taken by the Government to promote non-farm jobs for women in rural India 
besides the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme 
(MGNREGS); 
(d)  the steps taken by the Government to create an enabling environment for working 
women specifically in the rural areas; and 
(e)  the steps taken by the Government to encourage and financially support the married 
women to pursue higher education and employment in the rural areas? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT  
(SADHVI NIRANJAN JYOTI) 
 
(a) Till now, 36.28 lakh women from  Rural Households have been mobilized into 3.18 lakh 
Self Help Group s (SHGs) under Deendayal Antyodaya Yojany -Nationanl Rural Livelihood 
Mission (DAY -NRLM) in the States of Tamil Nadu and 45,459 women from  Rural 
Households have been mobilized into 4,606 SHGs in Karur constituency. 
(b) The details of funds allocated and release d under the NRLM to Tamil Nadu since 2014, 
year-wise are at Annexure-I. 
(c) The following   are scheme/components  under DAY -NRLM promote non -farm 
livelihoods  
  
(i) Start-up Village Entrepreneurship Programme : Start-up Village Entrepreneurship 
Programme (SVEP), the sub-scheme under the DAY-NRLM programme supports the 
Self-Help Group (SHG) or their family members to set -up small enterprises in the 
non-farm sector. SVEP develops an eco -system for enterprise development in rural 
areas, with SHG households, which in cludes: Community Enterprise Fund (CEF), a 
dedicated fund for providing loans to entrepreneurs, Cadre of Community Resource 
Persons-Enterprise Promotion (CRP-EP) for providing Business Support Services . 
  
         States have to submit proposals through supplementary Annual Action Plans (AAP) 
for funding support for   blocks to be covered under SVEP scheme under DAY -
NRLM. The funds allocation for each block depends on the number of enterprises to 
be supported in a block. The project duration is for a period  of four years from the 

approval. As on February, 2023, a total of 231,798 enterprises have been supported 
under the SVEP scheme. 
  
(ii) One Stop Facility (OSF) : OSF is a business facilitation -cum-incubation centres at 
the sub -district level to provide bus iness development services to existing nano -
enterprises on a growth track.   Under the One Stop Facility (OSF), as on February, 
2023, a total of 30,021 higher order enterprises have been supported across 13 
National Rural Economic Transformation Project(NRETP) States. 
  
(iii) Cluster development : Cluster development component includes improvement in 
parameters like increase in wages, turnover, employment, number of enterprises, 
exports etc. After scoping study and Details Survey Report (DSR) preparation & 
approval, the cluster projects are implemented. As on February, 2023, a total of 12 
cluster (artisanal and Sectoral) are approved across six States – Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, 
Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha and Uttar Pradesh. 
  
(iv) Incubators: The incubat or component is to scale up at least 100 -150 existing 
women-owned / women -led growth-oriented enterprises in a State and create models 
for replicability. Extensive mentorship support is provided to the selected enterprises 
under the incubator component. Th e enterprises supported will be in manufacturing 
and service sectors.   As on February, 2023, Incubator component is approved in 4 
States – Assam, Bihar, West Bengal and Karnataka.  
  
(v) Aajeevika Gramin Express Yojana (AGEY) : AGEY is a component   under DAY-
NRLM for providing safe, affordable and community monitored transport services to 
rural areas. The vehicles under AGEY are owned and operated by members of Self 
Help Group (SHG) networks. The scheme is intended to connect remote villages with 
services an d amenities including access to markets, education and health besides 
providing livelihood opportunities to SHG members. Till February, 2023, a total of 
2,208 vehicles are operational across 26 States/UT.   
 
(d)   DAY-NRLM is a flagship poverty alleviation  scheme. It aims to create sustainable 
livelihoods by targeting the marginalised/deprived community & build a strong social capital 
of the poor households. The Mission helps the women in rural areas to over come multiple 
dimensions of poverty through vario us inter

TO BE ANSWERED ON 14TH MARCH, 2023 
 
FISHING HARBOUR AND LANDING CENTRES 
 
2182.  SHRI VIJAY KUMAR DUBEY: 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING  
मत्स्यपालन, पशुपालन और डेयरी मंत्री be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details with regard to extension ofconcessional finance and Kisan Credit Card 
Facilityfor fisheries and animal husbandry under AnimalHusbandry Infrastructure 
Development Fund(AHIDF); and 
 
 
(b)  the details of projects related to enhancementof quality of fishes and export competition, 
providingstate-of-the-art infrastructure and facilities for fishing  harbour and landing 
centres? 
 
ANSWER 
 THE MINISTER FOR FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRYAND DAIRYING 
(SHRI PARSHOTTAM RUPALA) 
 
(a) :  The Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairyinghas launcheda‘Animal Husbandry 
Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF)’ with fund size of Rs.15000 crore, under which 3% 
interest subvention is being provided to all eligible entities (individual entrepreneurs, private 
companies, MSME, Farmers Producers Organizations  and section 8  companies) for Six 
categories  such as; (i) the dairy processing and value add ition infrastructure, (ii) meat 
processing and value addition infrastructure, (iii) Animal Feed Plant, (iv) Breed improvement 
technology and Breed multiplication farm , (v) Setting up of veterinary vaccine and drugs 
production facilities and (vi) Animal waste of wealth Management (Agri-waste Management). 
The other feature of the AHIDF includes; (i) loan up to 90% of the estimated/actual project 
cost, (ii) credit guarantee, (iii) maximum repayment period of 8 years including moratorium of 
2 years on principle amount and (iv) availability of convergence facilities etc.  
 

 The Government of India in 2018-19 extended the facility of Kisan Credit Card (KCC) 
to Animal Husbandry and Fishery farmers  to help them to meet their working capital needs. 
Under KCC facility, interest subvention is available for animal husbandry and fisheries farmers 
@ 2% per annum at the time of disbursal of loan and additional interest subvention @ 3% per 
annum in case of prompt repayment as Prompt Repayment Incentive. 
(b): The Pradhan Mantri  Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) being implemented by the 
Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Husbandry and  Dairying,to enhance India’s 
export competitiveness, provides supports for quality fish production, species diversification, 
promotion of export -oriented species, branding, standards and certification, training and 
capacity building, creation of post harvest infrastructure with emphasis on seamless cold chain 
and development of modern fishing harbours and fish landing centers.   
Under the PMMSY,a total of 26 fishing harbours and fish landing centres proposals at 
a total cost of Rs. 2158.65 crore have been approved including modernization and upgradation 
of existing 8 fishing harbours. In addition, Rs.1271.00 crore has  been sanctioned for the 
construction of 388 ice plant/cold storages, 588 fish feed mill/plants, 179 fish retail markets, 4 
State of Art Wholesale fish markets, 6034 fish kiosks including ornamental kiosks and 94 value 
added enterprise units. Further the Department of Fisheries, Government of India has also 
sanctioned 20,920 units of post-harvest fish transportation facilities viz., refrigerated (234) and 
insulated trucks (934), Live Fish Vending Centres (705), auto rickshaws (2783), motor cycles 
(8237) and bicycles with ice box (8027) at a total cost of Rs. 541.00 crore. 
 Further, to address the critical infrastructure requirements of fi sheries and aquaculture 
sectors, the Department of Fisheries, GoI during 2018 -19 has created the Fisheries and 
Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF) with a total fund size of Rs 7522.48 
crore to provide interest subvention up to 3% per annum for providing the concessional finance 
to States/UTs and private sector. Under FIDF, 21 Fishing Harbours to the tune of Rs. 4744.77 
crore has been approved for various coastal States namely Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, 
Gujarat and Maharashtra.

PMKSY BENEFIT TO FARMERS 
 
2185. SHRI DHANUSH M. KUMAR: 
 SHRI SELVAM G.: 
 SHRI C.N. ANNADURAI: 
 SHRIMATI MANJULATA MANDAL: 
 
Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
    
(a) whether the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Sampada Yojana (PMKSY) was launched with a view to 
benefit the farmers;  
 
(b) if so, the extent to which the farmers have actually been benefited since the launching of the 
yojana; 
 
(c) the challenges faced by the Government while implementing the Yojana; 
 
(d) whether the Government has achieved the objectives for which the PMKSY was launched, if so, 
the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor along with the corrective steps taken in this regard; 
 
(e) whether the Government has made any assessment regarding the works and performance of 
PMKSY during the last three years and the current year and if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(f) whether the Union Government has approved the proposals under the yojana for creation of 
Infrastructure for Agro-Processing Clusters of PMKSY, if so, the details thereof, State-wise? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI PRAHLAD SINGH PATEL) 
 
(a) & (b): Yes, the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Sampada Yojana (PMKSY) was launched by the Ministry of 
Food Processing Industries (MoFPI) with a view to benefit the farmers. PMKSY has helped in benefiting 
56.01 lakh farmers since inception of the Yojana. 
  
(c). The following are the challenges / problems that have been faced by the Government in the 
implementation of the Scheme. 
 
(i). Delay in submission of the statutory clearances/ certificates from the State Govt. regarding Consent 
to Establish (CTE), Consent to Operate (CTO), building plan approval, electricity connection etc. by 
the promoter/ implementing agency in relation to the project to the Ministry.  
 
(ii). Inadequate support from lending banks in disbursement of term loan to the approved projects. 
 
(iii) Upsurge of Covid -19 during 2020 and 2021 affected the implementation of projects. 
 
(d). Yes, the MoFPI has achieved the objectives of PMKSY. As on 28.02.2022 , 1375 projects have 
been approved with total grants-in-aid of Rs. 8536.14 crore , which has helped in creating processing 
capacity and preservation capacity of 292.88 LMT and 75.68 LMT respectively and generating 8.28 lakh 
employment under the scheme.  

   
(e). As on date, no impact assessment of PMKSY has been conducted by MoFPI. However, evaluation 
studies have been conducted for sub -schemes viz. Integrated Cold Chain and Value Addition 
Infrastructure, Food Safety & Quality Assurance Infrastructure, Creation/ Expansion of Food Processing 
and Preservation Capacities, Scheme for C reation of Infrastructure Development for Agro Processing 
Cluster and Scheme for Human Resource and Institutions – Skill Development and Research & 
Development of PMKSY. A brief of the studies conducted in respect of various component schemes of 
PMKSY are given in Annexure-I. 
 
(f). As on date, the MoFPI has approved 79 agro processing cluster (APC) projects under the 
component scheme – Creation of Infrastructure for Agro-Processing Clusters (APC scheme) of PMKSY. 
The State-wise details of APC projects approved under APC scheme is provided at Annexure-II.

2189.  SHRI S. VENKATESAN: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the number of Gram Panchayats adopted under the Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana 
(SAGY) from 2014-15 to 2022-23; 
(b)  whether the SAGY has been effective in ushering development in the selected Gram 
Panchayats; 
(c)  if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; 
(d)  whether it is true that the scheme has proved to be a non-starter even after eight years 
of its launch in some Gram Panchayats; 
(e)  if so, the details thereof and the reasons therefor; and 
(f)  the steps taken/being taken by the Government to develop the Gram Panchayats? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT  
(SADHVI NIRANJAN JYOTI) 
 
(a) :  The Hon’ble Members of Parliament (MPs) have adopted 3154 Gram Panchayats 
under the Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana (SAGY) from 2014-15 to 2022-23. 
 
(b) to (e) : The Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana has been very effective in ushering all round 
development in the Gram Panchayats selected by Hon'ble MPs as per guidelines of the 
scheme. The Gram Panchayats pr epare a Village Development Plan (VDP) in which the 
proposed activities are implemented through convergence of various schemes of the 
Government of India and the State Governments. It aims to trigger processes which lead to 
the holistic development of the identified Gram Panchayats. As on 7th March 2023, a total of 
2,625 SAGY Gram Panchayats have uploaded their Village Development Plans containing 
2,34,404 projects, out of which 1,63,632 projects have been completed. There is continuous 
development of these Gram Panchayats (GPs) under SAGY.  
 
(f) : The steps being taken by Government to develop the Gram Panchayats under SAGY is 
given in Annexure -I. 
 
****** 
 
  

 
Annexure-I 
Annexure-I referred in part (f) of reply to Rajya Sabha Unstarred Question No.2189 to 
be answered on 14/03/2023 
  
The steps being taken by Government to develop the Gram Panchayats under SAGY 
are as follows: 
 
(i) 26 Schemes of 17 Ministries of Government of India have been amended / 
appropriate advisories have been issued to accord priority to SAGY in respective 
schemes. 
(ii) The Ministry has brought out a compilation of 127 Central Sector and Centrally 
sponsored and 1806 State Schemes for convergence under SAGY. This document 
serves as a ready reckoner especially for the Members of Parliament, Distr ict and 
Village level officials about the different schemes for possible convergence at the 
GP level. 
(iii) The SAGY is reviewed periodically by the Ministry of Rural Development, which 
includes review by the Hon’ble Minister of Rural Development, Performance 
Review Committee, Common Review Missions, National Level Monitors, 
Concurrent Monitoring and Impact Assessment studies.  
(iv) Ministry has published a document named ‘SAHYOG’ as an indicative guidance 
document with the essential information on the existing social  security schemes 
collated from respective Ministries to enrich the knowledge of villagers and 
village level functionaries to achieve 100% enrollment into the social/ financial 
Security Schemes in SAGY Gram Panchayats.  
(v) The States have been requested to conduct the State Level Empowered Committee 
(SLEC) meetings headed by the Chief Secretary to review the implementation 
process and to ensure seamless convergence of schemes among different State 
Government Departments.  
(vi) The Ministry provides training on prep aration of VDP and the approaches to 
convergence of schemes to the Charge Officers and other stakeholders of the state 
who are coordinating the implementation at the local level and are fully 
responsible and accountable for the implementation of VDP.  
(vii) The parameters for dynamic ranking of Gram Panchayats have been recently 
developed and placed on the portal so as to instill competition amongst the 
selected SAGY GPs.  
(viii) MoRD has been holding orientation workshops of representatives of the Members 
of Parliament  for their capacity building and better coordination with State 
Governments in implementation of SAGY programme.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2192 
ANSWERED ON 14.03.2023 
 
TAX REDUCTION ON EVs 
 
2192. SHRI A. RAJA:  
SHRI A. GANESHAMURTHI:  
 
Will the Minister of HEAVY INDUSTRIES भारी उद्योग मंत्री be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of policies of the Government for incentivising manufacture of Electric 
Vehicles (EVs) in the country;  
 
(b) whether battery manufacturing capabilities and charg ing infrastructure facilities have 
improved during the last three years;  
 
(c) if so, the details thereof; and  
 
(d) whether tax reduction on EVs, exemption on stamp duty on purchase or lease of land 
obtained from the Government for the manufacturer is allowed so that people can go for EVs 
rather than petrol/ diesel vehicles and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR HEAVY INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI KRISHAN PAL GURJAR) 
 
(a):  Sir, the Ministry of Heavy Industries has given incentives to buyers and manufacturers of 
electric vehicles through following three schemes: 
 
i. Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of Hybrid and Electric Vehicles in India (FAME 
India): The Government notified Phase -II of FAME India Scheme for a period of five 
years commencing from 1 st April, 2019 with a total budgetary support of Rs. 10,000 
crore.  Under FAME-India Scheme phase-II, incentives are provided to buyers of electric 
vehicles in the form of an upfront reduction in the purchase price of electric vehicles.   
The incentive is linked to battery capacity i.e. Rs. 10,000/KWh for e-3W and e-4W with a 
cap 20% of the cost of vehicle.   Further, the incentive/ subsidies for e -2W has been 
increased to Rs. 15,000/KWh from Rs. 10,000/KWh with an increase in cap from 20% to 
40% of the cost of vehicle w.e.f. 11th June, 2021. 
 
ii. Production Linked Incentive (PLI)  Scheme for Automotive Sector:  The Government on 
15th Sep., 2021 approved the PLI Scheme for Automotive Sector with a budgetary outlay 
of Rs. 25,938 crores to support domestic manufacturing of vehicles.   Electric vehicles are 
covered under this PLI scheme. 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 
iii. PLI Scheme for Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC):  The Government on 12 th May, 2021 
approved PLI Scheme for manufacturing of ACC in the  country with a budgetary outlay 
of Rs. 18,100 crore.  The scheme envisages to establish a competitive ACC battery 
manufacturing set up in the country  for 30 GWh.  Additionally, 5GWh of niche ACC 
technologies is also covered under the Scheme. 
 
(b) & (c):  Yes, sir. Under PLI ACC Scheme, three entities have been awarded the ACC 
capacities i.e. Rajesh Exports Limited - 5 GWh, Ola Electric Mobility Private Limited - 20 GWh 
& Reliance New Energy Solar Limited - 5 GWh. 
 
Further, the Ministry of Heavy Industries has sanctioned 2,877 electric vehicle charging  
stations in 68 cities across 25 states/UTs  and 1576 charging stations across 9 Expressways and 
16 Highways under phase-II of FAME India Scheme has also been sanctioned.  
 
(d):  Sir, GST on electric vehicles has been reduced from 12% to 5%; GST on chargers/ 
charging stations for electric vehicles has been reduced from 18% to 5%.

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI AJAY KUMAR MISHRA) 
(a) & (b): The National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) compiles crime

2019-2021 are given in the statement at Annexure-I. 
‘Police’ and ‘Public Order’ are “State-List” subjects under the Seventh 
Schedule to the Constitution of India. Therefore, the primary responsibility 
for preventing and countering the crime of human trafficking, missing 
children and women vests with respective State Governments/Union 
Territories.  
The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has been supplementing the efforts of

and ‘State level conferences’ for sensitizing law officers/Police Officers, 
etc. on issues relating to trafficking. 
The Ministry of Women and Child Development has developed web portals 
namely “TrackChild” and “KhoyaPaya” for tracking missing children. The 
Ministry of Women & Child Development also provides support for an 
outreach service for children in distress through a dedicated toll free 
number 1098. They have also prepared Standard Operating Procedures 
(SOPs) for tracing missing children and has circulated the same to all 
States/UTs for dissemination to all stakeholders such as Police, Child 
Welfare Committee (CWCs) Juvenile Justice Boards (JJBs) etc. The 
Ministry of Railways, in collaboration with the Ministry of Women and Child 
Development and National Commission for Protection of Child Rights, has 
also issued a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for Railways to ensure 
Care and Protection of Children in contact with Railways.

National University for Cooperative Training 
 
2198.  SHRI G.M. SIDDESHWAR: 
Will the Minister of COOPERATION (सहकाįरता मंũी) be pleased to state: 
(a)  whether the Government proposes to set up a National University that offers 
cooperative training courses in its colleges in different parts of the country, including 
Karnataka and if so, the details thereof; 
  
(b) whether the Government is also coming up with a new cooperative policy soon to 
expand business in the cooperation sector in the foreseeable future; and 
 
(c) if so, the details thereof and progress made in this regard, State-wise? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF COOPERATION  
सहकाįरता मंũी (SHRI AMIT SHAH) 
 
(a) to (c): Yes, sir. There is a need for establishment of a Cooperative University to firmly 
deepen the foundations of cooperative movement in the country. Efforts are being made in 
this direction. 
 
The Ministry is in the process of formulating the New National Cooperation Policy. A 
national-level committee has been constituted on 2nd September 2022 under the chairmanship 
of Shri Suresh Prabhakar Prabhu, consisting of experts from the cooperative sector, 
representatives from National/ State/ District/ Primary level cooperative societies, Secretaries 
(Cooperation) and RCSs from States/UTs, officers from Central Ministries/ Departments to 
formulate the New National Cooperation Policy. The formulation of New National 
Cooperation Policy will help realize the vision of 'Sahakar se Samriddhi', promoting the 
cooperative-based economic development model, strengthening the cooperative movement in 
the country and deepening its reach upto the grassroots. In this regard, consultations were 
held earlier with stakeholders and suggestions were invited from the Central 
Ministries/Departments, States/UTs, National Cooperative Federations, Institutions and also 
from the general public. The National level committee will analyse the collated feedback, 
policy suggestions & recommendations to formulate the draft of the new Policy.

2200.  SHRI JAYANT SINHA: 
SHRI BHOLANATH (B.P. SAROJ): 
SHRI ASHOK KUMAR RAWAT: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS  WELFARE क ृ षि एवं ककसान  कल्याण मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the number of beneficiaries and mandis registered under National Agricultural Market 
(eNAM) till date, State/UT-wise particularly in the State of Uttar Pradesh; 
(b)  the funds allocated and utilized for eNAM, State/UT-wise and year-wise; 
(c)  the measures taken by the Government to register more farmers under eNAM; 
(d)  the details of the initiatives of the Government to introduce more mandis to the online 
trading platform and the targets set thereof; 
(e)  whether the eNAM platform has helped  farmers from Uttar Pradesh to increase their 
revenue and double their income, if so, the details thereof; and 
(f)  the details of work done/being done under  eNAM and the updated status thereon in 
the State of  Uttar Pradesh particularly in the Parliamentary  Constituency of Misrikh?
  
 
ANSWER  
 
MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
क ृ षि एवं ककसान  कल्याण मंत्री     (SHRI NARENDRA SINGH TOMAR) 
(a): National Agriculture Market (e -NAM) is a virtual platform integrating physical 
wholesale mandis/ markets of different States/ Union Territories (UTs) to facilitate online 
trading of agricultural commodities through transparent price discovery method to enable 
farmers to realize better remunerative prices for their produce.  The number of beneficiaries 
viz. farmers and traders registered and mandis integrated under National Agricultural Market 
(eNAM) till date, State/UT-wise including the State of Uttar Pradesh is at Annexure – I. 
 
(b): The funds released for eNAM, State/UT -wise and year -wise as on 28.02.2023 is at 
Annexure – II. 
 

(c): Various measures have been taken to register more number of farmers, some of 
which are as follows :- 
 
i. User friendly portal and mobile app has been developed wherein user can register 
online. Portal and mobile app is freely downloadable and are available in 12 
languages. 
ii. Online Tutorials and user guide is available on e -NAM website ( www.enam.gov.in) 
for benefit of users which provides detail information on registration and other 
process. 
iii. Helpdesk support  : A toll free number ( 1800 2700 224) and email support 
(enam.helpdesk@gmail.com) is available to assist users regarding e -NAM 
registration and other queries. 
iv. Stakeholder trainings for Farmers, Traders, Farmer Producer Organisations and 
mandis staff etc are conducted regularly to create awareness and hand -holding 
regarding e-NAM portal.  
v. Uttar Pradesh State A griculture Marketing Board celebrates “e -NAM diwas” at every 
e-NAM integrated mandi periodically to create awareness and eventually register 
more farmers on e-NAM. 
 
(d): The Government is encouraging States/UTs to submit proposal s along with Detailed 
Project Reports ( DPRs) to integrate more mandis on e -NAM. Operational Guideline 
alongwith DPR format are available on e-NAM website (www.enam.gov.in).  
 
(e): As per the evaluation Report of CCS National Institute of Agricultural Marketing 
(NIAM) on “performance evaluation of National Agriculture Market” (October, 2020), the 
platform helps in creating a unified market through online trading both at State & National 
levels. This e-NAM concept further ensures various ben efits like streamlining of procedures 
across the integrated markets, promotes real time price discovery based on actual demand 
and supply, removes information asymmetry between buyers and sellers, promotes 
transparency in auction process, promotes access t o a nation -wide market for the farmer 
along with prices commensurate with quality of produce and online payment of sales 
proceeds. 
 
(f): In the State of Uttar Pradesh, as on 09.03.2023 , a total of 125 mandis have been 
integrated on e -NAM platform and a tot al no. of 3303963 farmers and 38771 traders have 
been registered. Out of the above, in the Parliamentary Constituency of Misrikh, two mandis 
at Madhoganj and Sandila have been integrated on e -NAM platform and a total of 42203 
farmers and 177 traders have been registered.

2201.  SHRI MAHABALI SINGH: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the total expenditure made under the Garib Kalyan Rozgar Abhiyan (GKRA); 
(b)  the details of the basic infrastructure developed under GKRA; and 
(c)  the details of the new steps taken in Rohtas, Bihar to promote skill and 
entrepreneurship for rural development? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT  
(SADHVI NIRANJAN JYOTI) 
 
(a)    In the wake of Covid-19 pandemic, Government of India launched Garib Kalyan Rojgar 
Abhiyaan (GKRA) of 125 days on 20th June, 2020 to boost employment and livelihood 
opportunities for returnee migrant workers and similarly affected citizens in rural areas. The 
GKRA ended on 22nd October, 2020 and a total of 50.78 crore person-days employment were 
generated with a total expenditure of Rs. 39,293 crores during the Abhiyaan. 
  
(b)     The details of achievements/works completed under the GKRA are given at Annexure. 
  
(c)    There are multiple steps taken by the Government to create employment in rural areas. 
Some of the notable initiatives are listed below: 
  
(i)   Project ‘UNNATI’, launched in December 2019 by Government of India, is a 
skilling project that intends to upgrade the skill base of the Mahatma Gandhi 
National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (Mahatma Gandhi NR EGS) 
workers, and thereby improve their livelihoods so that they can move from the 
current partial employment to full employment.  
  
(ii) There are two skill development programmes for rural youth under Deendayal 
Antyodaya Yojana -National Rural Livelihoods  Mission (DAY -NRLM), namely, 
Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU -GKY) and Rural Self 
Employment Training Institutes (RSETIs). Both these programmes are aimed at 
increasing employability of rural youth, either for wage employment or self -
employment. 
  
(iii)  Start-up Village Entrepreneurship Programme (SVEP) under DAY -NRLM 
programme supports the Self-Help Groups and their family members to set-up small 
enterprises in the non-farm sector. 
  
(iv) The Ministry has launched the Rural Mason Training (RMT) program under the 
Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana - Gramin (PMAY -G) to address the issue of 
insufficient number of skilled masons for construction of quality PMAY -G houses. 
The initiative additionall y generates livelihood opportunities for the rural 
workforce.

SMALL AND MARGINAL FARMERS UNDER PMFBY 
 
2202. COL. RAJYAVARDHAN RATHORE: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृषि एवं कक सान क ल्याण मंत्री  
be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the number of marginal and small farmers insured under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima 
Yojana (PMFBY) in the country as of 2023, State-wise particularly in Rajasthan;  
(b) whether climate change is leading to new diseases affecting crop health and farm -
insurance claims have risen due to extensive crop damage caused by extreme weather 
conditions;  
(c) the details of the sums paid as insurance payouts to farmers affected by the above, year -
wise and State-wise for the past three years; and  
(d) the number of  farmers claiming farm insurance due to crop damage in the past three 
years and the average per capita compensation paid to them, year-wise? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
क ृषि एवं कक सान क ल्याण मंत्री  (SHRI NARENDRA SINGH TOMAR) 
 
(a) to (d) : State -wise details of small & marginal farmers applications enrolled during 2022 -
23 under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) are given in Annexure-I. 
 It is true that the climate change is affecting the crop health and production.  But 
Government is committed to provide financial security to farmers against the crop loss due to 
adverse climatic conditions.   In order to secure the farmers against the crop yield losses due 
to natural risks/calamities, adverse weather conditions, pests & di seases etc. two major crop 
insurance schemes namely, Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) and Restructured 
Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme (RWBCIS) are being implemented by the 
Government.   PMFBY provides  comprehensive risk coverage from pre -sowing to post 
harvest losses against non -preventable natural risks.  The RWBCIS provides indemnification 
for likely crop losses due to deviation in weather indices.    

 Only those farmers who insure their crops under th e PMFBY/RWBCIS are eligible for 
the claims in case of any damage occurred to their crops as per the procedure defined in the 
Operational Guidelines of the Scheme, therefore,  the question of  per  capita compensation 
does not arise.   State-wise details of farmer applications enrolled , farmer applications paid 
claims and claims paid during 2019-20 to 2021-22 under PMFBY are given in Annexure-II.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2204 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 14TH MARCH, 2023 
 
TESTING OF GENETICALLY MODIFIED CROPS 
 
2204:   SHRI K. NAVASKANI: 
 
Will the MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ षि एवं ककसान  कल्याण मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a)     whether it is mandatory to rigorously test Genetically Modified (GM) crops for safety on a 
case-to-case basis before they are released for general cultivation; 
 
(b)      if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(c)     if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
 
 
MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
 
क ृ षि एवं ककसान  कल्याण मंत्री  (SHRI NARENDRA SINGH TOMAR) 
 
(a) to (c) There is a well established regulatory framework for approval of Genetically 
Modified (GM) crops as per “Rules for the Manufacture/Use/Import/Export and Storage of 
Hazardous Microorganisms, Genetically Engineered Organisms or Cells, 1989” under the 
Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 in the Country. 
 
Evaluation of each application of GM cro p is done mandatorily on a case -to-case basis 
after a thorough examination of health, environment, food and feed safety assessment studies 
undertaken in a systematic and scientific manner as per prescribed guidelines, manuals and 
standard operating procedu res stipulated by various regulatory agencies under the Rules, 
1989 from time to time. The data generated by the applicants is reviewed at every step in the 
development process of GM crops by various Statutory Committees under the Rules, 1989 
such as Insti tutional Biosafety Committee, Review Committee on Genetic Manipulation and 
Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee. 
 

A series of guidelines and protocols have been issued by Department of Biotechnology 
and Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Chang e relating to Genetically Modified 
Organisms and product thereof as under: 
 
i. Recombinant DNA Safety Guidelines, 1990 
ii. Revised Guidelines for Research in Transgenic Plants, 1998 
iii. Guidelines for the Safety Assessment of Foods Derived from Genetically Engineered  
Plants, 2008 
iv. Guidelines for the monitoring of Confined Field Trials of Regulated, Genetically 
Engineered (GE) Plants, 2008 
v. Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for Confined Field Trials of Regulated, 
Genetically Engineered (GE) Plants, 2008 
vi. Protocol for Food and Feed Safety Assessment of GE crops, 2008 
vii. Guidelines and Handbook for Institutional Bio-safety Committees (IBSCs), 2011 
viii. Environmental Risk Assessment of Genetically Engineered Plants: A Guide for 
Stakeholders, 2016 
ix. Guidelines for the E nvironmental Risk Assessment of Genetically Engineered Plants, 
2016. 
x. Risk Analysis Framework, 2016.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF COOPERATION

Implementation of Central Sector Schemes through Cooperative Organizations 
 
†2205. SHRI DULAL CHANDRA GOSWAMI: 
 
Will the Minister of COOPERATION (सहकाįरता मंũी) be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Central sector schemes are being implemented through cooperative organisations 
working at National and State level for farmers’ benefit; 
(b) if so, the details of the schemes; and 
(c) if not, whether the Government proposes to formulate any scheme for providing training and also 
for distribution of fertilizers and seeds in Bihar through national level cooperative societies and 
thereby strengthening the cooperative movement and providing benefits to the farmers? 
 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF COOPERATION 
सहकाįरता मंũी (SHRI AMIT SHAH) 
 
(a) to (c): In order to realize the vision ‘from cooperation to prosperity’, strengthening of co-
operative movement in the country, deepening its reach up to the grassroots and promotion of 
cooperative ecosystem in various sectors including the agriculture sector, government is 
implementing various schemes – central sector and centrally sponsored schemes, programmes and 
initiatives  across the country, including Bihar, through the instrumentation of central nodal agencies, 
state governments, national, state and district level cooperative federations, primary cooperative 
societies etc. for the benefit of the farmers. 
 
In this regard, Ministry of Cooperation, since its formation in July, 2021, has taken many initiatives 
such as: 
1. Computerization of PACS: Process to onboard 63,000 PACS on an ERP based common 
national software with an outlay of ₹2,516 Crore started.  

2. Model byelaws for PACS: Model byelaws prepared and circulated for their adoption as per the 
respective State Cooperatives Act to enable PACS to undertake more than 25 business 
activities like dairy, fishery, setting up of godowns, LPG/ Petrol/ Green energy distribution 
agency, banking correspondents, CSC, etc. 
3. PACS as Common Service Centres (CSC): MoU signed between Ministry of Cooperation, 
Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, NABARD and CSC - SPV to facilitate 
functioning of PACS as CSCs to improve their viability, provide e-services at village level and 
generate employment. 
4. National Cooperative Database: Preparation of an authentic and updated data repository of 
cooperatives in the country started to facilitate stakeholders in policy making and 
implementation.  
5. Establishment of Multi-Purpose PACS, Dairy and Fisheries Cooperative Societies in every 
Panchayat/Village: A plan has been approved by the Government to set up 2 lakh new multi-
purpose PACS, dairy and fisheries cooperatives covering every Panchayat/Village in the next 
five years by taking advantage of various existing schemes. 
6. National Cooperative Policy: A National level committee comprising of experts and 
stakeholders drawn from all over the Country constituted to formulate the New Cooperation 
Policy to create an enabling ecosystem to realize the vision of ‘Sahakar-se-Samriddhi’. 
7. Amendment of MSCS Act, 2002: Bill introduced in the Parliament to amend the centrally 
administered MSCS Act, 2002 to incorporate provisions of 97th Constitutional Amendment, 
strengthen governance, enhance transparency, increase accountability and reform electoral 
process in the Multi State Cooperative Societies. 
8. National Cooperative Development Corporation: New schemes for cooperatives launched by 
NCDC in various sectors such as ‘Swayam shakti Sahkar’ for SHG; ‘Deerghavadhi Krishak 
Sahkar’ for long term agricultural credit; ‘Dairy Sahkar’ for dairy and ‘Neel Sahkar’ for 
fisheries. Total financial assistance of Rs. 34,221 Crores disbursed in FY 2021-22. 
9. Member Lending Institutions in Credit Guarantee Fund Trust: Non-scheduled UCBs, StCBs 
and DCCBs notified as MLIs in CGTMSE Scheme to increase share of cooperatives in 
lending. 
10. Cooperatives as ‘buyers’ on GeM portal: Cooperatives permitted to register as ‘buyer’ on 
GeM, enabling them to procure goods and services from nearly 40 lakh vendors to facilitate 
economical purchases and greater transparency. 
11. Reduction in surcharge on cooperative societies: Surcharge reduced from 12 % to 7% for co-
operative societies having income between Rs. 1 to 10 Cr.  

12. Reduction in Minimum Alternate Tax: MAT reduced for cooperatives from 18.5% to 15%. 
13. Relief under Section 269ST of IT Act: A clarification has been issued to remove difficulties in 
cash transactions by cooperatives under Section 269ST of IT Act. 
14. Lowering tax rate for new cooperatives: Announcement made in the Union Budget 2023-24 to 
charge flat lower tax rate of 15%, compared with current rate of upto 30% plus surcharge, for 
new cooperatives commencing manufacturing activities till March 31, 2024.  
15. Increase in limit of deposits and loans in cash by PAC

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2208 
 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 14TH MARCH, 2023/ PHALGUNA 23, 1944 (SAKA) 
 
LOSS OF CATTLE AND LIVESTOCK DUE TO FLOODS 
 
2208.  SHRI DUSHYANT SINGH: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the details of loss of cattle and livestock due  to the floods in Rajasthan 
during August 2022, district-wise; 
 
(b) whether the Government intends to provide  assistance with respect to 
animal losses during a  natural disaster as per the actual number of cattle  
loss; 
 
(c) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; 
 
(d) whether the Government intends to amend  SDRF norms to include  
Goshalas as cattle camps and allow relief assistance for all the cattle kept in 
these Goshalas; and 
 
(e) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
 
(SHRI NITYANAND RAI) 
(a) to (e): Calamity-wise and district -wise losses are not  centrally 
maintained by this Ministry.  However, a s per information received from the 
State Government of Rajasthan, 184 cattles have been reported lost during 
south-west monsoon 2022.   
 

-2- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 2208 FOR 14.03.2023 
 
The primary responsibility for disaster management rests with the States.  
The concerned State Governments undertake relief operations in the event of 
natural calamities from the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF), which are 
already placed at its disposal  in accordance with the Government of India 
approved items & norms of assistance. The Government of India supplements 
their efforts by providing assistance from the National Disaster Response 
Fund (NDRF) by following the laid down procedure.  Financial ass istance 
under SDRF/ NDRF in the event of natural calamities is by way of relief and 
not for compensation of loss as suffered/ claimed.  
With regard to Goshalas, it is stated that as per revised list of items & norms, 
assistance is admissible for the existi ng Goshalas, if authorized by the State 
Government by Notification or Government Order, to act as a cattle camp 
subject to the following conditions:- 
(i) During the period of calamity, District Administration will assess the 
requirement of cattle shelter and n umber of gaushala required to be 
notified as cattle shelter in the District/ Tehsil.  After obtaining the 
base-line information on the cattle already sheltered and the number of 
more cattle it can accommodate, Gaushala may be notified as cattle 
shelter. 
 
 

-3- 
L.S.US.Q.NO. 2208 FOR 14.03.2023 
 
(ii) The notified gaushala shall maintain a separate account of the 
additional cattle belonging to Small and Marginal Farmers (SMF) and 
landless labourers for the notified drought period.  The consolidated list 
of SMF and landless beneficiaries with number and types of animals will 
be displayed on the notice board of Gram Panchayat, Block, Tehsil and 
in the office of Sub-Divisional Magistrate and District Magistrate as well 
as State/ District web -site for the purpose of veri fication and social 
audit. 
(iii) SDRF funds will only be released to such notified gaushala on 
reimbursement basis and will be limited to list of individual 
beneficiaries notified as in Sl. No. (ii) above.

VILLAGES COVERED BY NRLM 
 
2210.  DR. DNV SENTHILKUMAR S.: 
SHRIMATI SUPRIYA SULE: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the number of villages covered by the National Rural Livelihood Mission (NRLM) in 
the States of Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra; 
(b)  whether the Government has any data to boost Self Help Groups (SHGs) in rural 
economies across States, if so, the details thereof, State-wise and district-wise 
particularly in Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra; 
(c)  whether NRLM has been successful in providing training to the youth from backward/ 
remote villages living below poverty line during the last three years in the States of 
Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra; 
(d)  if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; 
(e)  the amount of funds allocated by the Government during the last three years under 
NRLM to Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu and North Eastern Region; and 
(f)  the number of beneficiaries under the Mission in the States of Tamil Nadu and 
Maharashtra? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT  
(SADHVI NIRANJAN JYOTI) 
 
(a)  A total of 51,479 and 38,039 villages have been   covered under Deendayal Antyodaya 
Yojana-National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY -NRLM) in the State of Tamil Nadu and 
Maharashtra respectively till 28th February 2023 . 
 
(b)   DAY-NRLM is a flagship poverty alleviation scheme.   It aims to create sustainable 
livelihoods by targeting the marginalised/deprived community & build a strong social capital of the 
poor households. Under the Mission , financial grant   is being  provided to Self Help Groups(SHGs) 
in the form of   Revolving Fund (RF)  and Community Investment   Fund (CIF) and    SHGs are also 
being facilitated   to access Bank loans. These funds are utilised by SHG members for the their 
consumption needs and also   to  take up   income generation activities. The details of   Bank loan 
disbursed to SHGs and the RF and CIF amount provided to the SHGs in the last two   financial  year  
and current financial year are given at Annexure-I.  
 
(c) & (d)   Ministry of Rural Development is  implementing the following two sub schemes under 
DAY-NRLM in the field of skill development for rural poor youth (including those from backward/ 
remote villages) :-  
 
I. Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU -GKY) which is a placement 
linked skill development program for wage employment. 
II. Skill development through Rural Self Employment Training Institutes (RSETIs) is enabling a

NATIONAL LIVESTOCK MISSION 
2117.  DR. SHRIKANT EKNATH SHINDE:  
DR. HEENA VIJAYKUMAR GAVIT:  
DR. SUJAY RADHAKRISHNA VIKHE PATIL:  
SHRI UNMESH BHAIYYASAHEB PATIL:  
PROF. RITA BAHUGUNA JOSHI:  
DR. KRISHNA PAL SINGH YADAV:  
 
Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING  
मत्स्यपालन, पशुपालन और डेयरी मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of main aims and objectives of National Livestock Mission (NLM);  
(b) whether NLM had been able to achieve its aims and objectives and if so, the details thereof;  
(c) the details of steps taken by the Government to im prove the quality and production of fodder 
in the country;  
(d) the details of initiative taken by the Government to conserve and for genetically upgrading of 
indigenous breeds; and  
(e) the total amount released and spent by the Government for NLM during each of the last three 
years and the current year? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER FOR FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING 
(SHRI PARSHOTTAM RUPALA) 
 
(a) The main aims and objective s of the Realigned National Livestock Mission  which is 
being implemented  since 2021 -22 are to bring sharp focus on entrepreneurship and breed 
improvement in poultry, sheep, goat and piggery including feed and fodder development , 
extension & innovation and the livestock insurance as well. 
 
 
 

(b)  The National Livestock Mission is under implementation since 2014.  The erstwhile 
National Livestock Mission scheme was having 50 activities on which the States need to 
prioritize the activities depending on the demand. Therefore, activities under erstwhile National 
Livestock Mission were not implemented equally across the country . The Niti Aayog evaluated 
the erstwhile National Livestock Mission and suggested for modification as there was very little 
progress made by the States und er National Livestock Mission. They also advised that the 
scheme should be focused and targeted towards employment generation, entrepreneurship 
development, feed and fodder development, genetic upgradation, extension  & innovation  and 
livestock insurance. Accordingly, the National Livestock Mission scheme has been realigned and 
is being implemented since 2021-22 after its approval by the Cabinet on 14.07.2021. The present 
National Livestock Mission is  being successfully implem ented with huge demand  and 
acceptability. 
 
(c) Under the Sub Mission on Feed and Fodder Development under the realigned National 
Livestock Mission, 100% financial assistance is provided for quality seed production of high 
yielding fodder varieties promoting fodder crop as a cash crop thereby diversifying more area 
under the fodder crops.  
 
Further Entrepreneurial activities in feed and fodder is also operational under National Livestock 
Mission where in the private entrepreneurs, S elf Help Groups (SHG) , F armers Cooperative
